Retrieve surveillance data from CDC AtlasPlus

Source: R/get_atlas.R
get_atlas.Rd

get_atlas() provides a programmatic interface to the CDC AtlasPlus platform, returning case counts, population denominators, and rates for HIV, sexually transmitted infections (STIs), viral hepatitis and tuberculosis surveillance. The function submits a payload to the AtlasPlus data endpoint and parses the response into a tidy tibble.

Usage

get_atlas(
  disease,
  geography,
  year,
  stratify_by = NULL,
  extrapolate_to_tract = deprecated(),
  refresh = FALSE
)

Arguments

disease

A single disease name (e.g. "gonorrhea"). Multiple diseases are not currently supported in a single request.

geography

Character scalar. One of "national", "region" (HIV estimates only), "state", "county" (not hepatitis or congenital syphilis), or "msa" ("hiv" only), as AtlasPlus offers them.

year

Integer vector of years, from 2000 to the latest year in the package's copy of CDC's code table (2025 in this version). CDC lists a year before every disease has data for it; such a request returns no data. Can be a single year (e.g., 2022) or a sequence (e.g., 2018:2022).

stratify_by

Optional character vector. Zero, one, or two of "age", "race", "sex". If NULL, totals (unstratified) are returned. Each disease has its own age groups, as AtlasPlus offers them: 13-24 to 65+ for "hiv" and "estimate"; 0-14, 15-19 and so on to 65+ for the other diseases, plus "Unknown" for chlamydia, gonorrhea and adult syphilis. Race groups also differ: hepatitis has Asian/Pacific Islander and Other in place of Asian, Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander and Multiracial; HIV and the HIV estimates have no Unknown group. Congenital syphilis can't be stratified.

extrapolate_to_tract

No longer supported. Use impute_suppressed() and then extrapolate_from_county().

refresh

If TRUE, download the data again from CDC even if a saved copy is less than 30 days old, and save the new copy. For county data this also drops the saved state totals that impute_suppressed(), no_county_cases() and extrapolate_from_county() use with them, so those are downloaded again too. Default FALSE.

Value

A tibble with the following columns:

indicator

Disease/condition name (factor)

year

Calendar year (numeric)

geography

Geographic unit name (factor)

data_status

Data quality flags (factor)

race_ethnicity

Race/ethnicity category (factor, if stratified)

sex

Sex category (factor, if stratified)

age

Age group (factor, if stratified)

transmission

Transmission category (factor)

rate100000

Rate per 100,000 population (numeric): per 100,000 people aged 13 and older for HIV, and per 100,000 live births for congenital syphilis. For Knowledge of Status, the percentage of people with HIV who know their status.

cases

Case count (numeric). For Knowledge of Status, the number who know their status.

population

Population denominator (numeric). For Knowledge of Status, estimated HIV prevalence.

lowerci_rate, upperci_rate

95% CI bounds for rate100000 (numeric); for Knowledge of Status, of the percentage. Usually empty (NA) for reported cases; given for the modeled estimates.

rse

Relative standard error (numeric)

lowerci_cases, upperci_cases

95% CI bounds for cases (numeric). Given for estimated HIV incidence and prevalence; usually empty (NA) for reported cases and for Knowledge of Status.

fips

FIPS code (character)

Columns and naming conventions may differ depending on CDC schema changes. The function attempts to standardize but does not guarantee historical compatibility for all years.

Details

The function supports multiple diseases, geographic levels, year ranges, and optional stratification. Stratified queries expand results into all requested combinations (e.g., age by race). When possible, numeric fields are returned as double and identifiers as character.

get_atlas() only downloads. For census tract or block group estimates, pass county data to impute_suppressed() and then extrapolate_from_county():

county <- get_atlas("hiv", "county", 2022, stratify_by = "sex")
county <- impute_suppressed(county)
no_county_cases(county)
tracts <- extrapolate_from_county(county)

Supported diseases

Some values return more than one indicator; the indicator column says which row is which.

  • "chlamydia"

  • "gonorrhea"

  • "adult syphilis": three indicators, one per stage: primary and secondary syphilis; early non-primary, non-secondary syphilis; and syphilis of unknown duration or late syphilis.

  • "congenital syphilis"

  • "tuberculosis"

  • "hiv": two indicators, HIV diagnoses (new diagnoses in the year) and HIV prevalence (people living with diagnosed HIV).

  • "estimate": three modeled HIV indicators: estimated HIV incidence, estimated HIV prevalence (diagnosed and undiagnosed), and Knowledge of Status. Knowledge of Status is a percentage, not a count. AtlasPlus says CDC has postponed release of estimates for HIV incidence and HIV prevalence, so recent years may be missing; check AtlasPlus for what is available.

  • "hepatitis": three indicators: hepatitis A, acute hepatitis B and acute hepatitis C.

HIV indicators cover people aged 13 and older; the other diseases cover all ages.

Geography

  • "national"

  • "region": the four Census regions (Northeast, Midwest, South, West) and U.S. territories and freely associated states. Only for disease = "estimate": CDC returns regions only for its HIV estimates. The fips column holds CDC's own codes for these, not Census FIPS codes.

  • "state"

  • "county"

  • "msa" (metropolitan statistical area)

Stratification The CDC AtlasPlus API supports stratification by one or two dimensions:

  • "age"

  • "race"

  • "sex"

Stratification increases the number of returned rows. For example, stratify_by = c("race", "sex") returns the race × sex combinations CDC offers for each geography-year pair. CDC doesn't offer every disease, geography and stratification together (hepatitis by sex at state level, for example); such a request stops with "CDC AtlasPlus returned no data". If CDC returns some of a disease's indicators but not others, a warning names the missing ones.

This function is a reverse-engineered wrapper around the AtlasPlus public query system. The CDC does not publish an official API specification, and internal identifiers may change without notice. If the CDC modifies the backend schema, requests may fail. Please report issues via GitHub.

Saved downloads

Data are requested from CDC one disease and one year at a time (and for counties, one state at a time). Each response is saved in the folder given by tools::R_user_dir("CDCAtlas", "cache") and reused for 30 days, so data already downloaded, alone or as part of a larger request, aren't downloaded again. After 30 days the data are downloaded again, which picks up any revisions CDC has made. Use refresh = TRUE to download them sooner, or clear_atlas_cache() to delete every saved response.

See also

impute_suppressed() and extrapolate_from_county() for tract and block group estimates from county data.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# National gonorrhea rates for 2018–2022
get_atlas(disease = "gonorrhea", geography = "national", year = 2018:2022)

# State-level chlamydia, stratified by race
get_atlas(
  disease = "chlamydia",
  geography = "state",
  year = 2022,
  stratify_by = "race"
)

# County gonorrhea, shared across census tracts
county <- get_atlas(disease = "gonorrhea", geography = "county", year = 2022)
tracts <- extrapolate_from_county(impute_suppressed(county))
} # }
